notes:
the destination - lean bulk is the vehicle. Deadline advanced after 160x8 on Jul 20 (e1RM ~203). Pace: e1RM 210 by Sep 1, 215 by Oct 1, 220 by Nov 1, 225 by Dec 1. Stretch: 235 by Jan 15, 2027. The risk window is Oct-Dec (historical layoff season).

STATUS 8/31 (push, 175 repeat as prescribed): 175 x 7,5 - e1RM 215.83, up from 210.0 on 8/27. This CLEARS THE OCT 1 GATE (215) a month early, having cleared the Sep 1 gate (210) four days early. Required rate to 225 by Dec 1 falls from 1.11 to 0.70 e1RM/wk against a trailing 8/16-8/31 actual of ~3.2/wk. Bench is no longer the goal in trouble, but it is still the tightest.
WHAT ACTUALLY MOVED IT: parking the load. The third set was prescribed and NOT run (Adam confirmed 8/31) - he lifted two sets, as always. So +5.8 e1RM in four days is attributable to holding 175 alone, versus +1.0 e1RM across the whole 8/07-8/27 stretch of buying load with reps. Plan item 1 is validated; plan item 2 is still untested.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE THIRD SET: it is now an accelerator, not a rescue. Add it, but if bench stalls once it is in, DROP THE THIRD SET, not the load - parking is the intervention with evidence behind it.
GRADUATION CRITERION CLARIFIED 8/31: '175 until it is 8,7' means 8,7 ON THE FIRST TWO SETS. Adding a third set must not move the goalposts on the jump to 180; the third set's reps are whatever they are.
8/31 ACCESSORY NOTE: load rose on four of five accessories in one session while bench set count did not - backwards relative to the diagnosis. Increment size predicted every result: the cable pushdown at +10% (30->33) held 7,7, while both dumbbell lifts at +20% regressed (lateral raise 25s 10,10,10 -> 30s 7,6,6; skull crusher 25 10,10 -> 30 for 5, dropped to 25 for 10). 5 lb is the smallest DB step at 25 lb, so +20% is a hardware limit, not a judgment error. HOLD ALL ACCESSORY LOADS next push day so the third bench set is the only new variable - Adam's own 8/23 rule.


DIAGNOSIS 8/28: bench stalled because Adam applied a different progression rule than squat. Bench 8/07-8/27 went 165x8,6 -> 165x8,7 -> 170x7,5 -> 175x6,5: +10 lb of bar, +1.0 e1RM. He is buying load with reps ~1:1. Squat over the same window sat on 225 for FOUR sessions (6,6 / 7,6 / 8,6 / 8,7) before jumping to 235, and gained 25 e1RM. Same athlete, same month, same creatine - the rule is the only difference. Precedent: 165 took 17 days to consolidate (6,4 on 7/30 -> 8,7 on 8/16).

PLAN (set 8/28, supersedes ad-hoc load calls):
1. PARK AT 175 until it is 8,7. Do not jump on a session that did not earn it. 175x8,7 = e1RM 221.7 on its own, ~90% of the remaining gap. Expect ~17 days by the 165 precedent, so ~mid-Sep. Then 180 (180x8,7 = 228) clears 225 in early October with two months of buffer.
2. ADD A THIRD WORKING SET. Adam's own 8/23 note: 'the volume problem is bench-specific.' Row gets 3 sets and just hit 175x8,8,7; bench gets 2. Do not change load and set count in the same session - he correctly pushed back on that once already (8/23).
3. HEAVY SINGLES GO AT THE FRONT OF PUSH DAY, BEFORE the working sets - never after, and never as a separate 4th session. Rationale: a single is skill + max CNS effort and needs to be fresh; done after 3x8 it rehearses a broken groove and the number is meaningless for calibration. One single costs the working sets almost nothing in the reverse direction. A 4th day is recovery Adam does not have (HRV 41.0 on 8/27, 2nd-lowest in series) for ~5 min of work.
   Now -> mid-Sep: NO singles. Consolidating 175 is the higher-value job.
   Mid-Sep -> early Oct: open with a top set of 3 @ RPE 8, ~190, then the 6-8 work.
   Oct -> mid-Nov: top SINGLE @ RPE 8-9 before working sets, every push day. Start ~200 and climb. Trim backoff volume as singles get heavy.
   Late Nov: one true attempt, ~2 weeks before the test window so he can recover from it.
   Throughout: RPE 8-9, NOT true maxes. Weekly maxing is how this stalls in October.
4. SPOTTER OR SAFETY PINS mandatory once singles exceed ~190. Adam has never failed a rep in 170 logged sessions because he has never trained below 5 reps - that changes in October. He should know what a miss feels like before it happens under 215.

CAVEAT: e1RM 225 is NOT a tested 225. Every one of 170 logged sessions is 6-8 reps (accessories 10s); Epley off 8-rep sets overestimates true 1RM for a lifter with no heavy-single practice. The rep transition below is the mechanism that closes that gap - start it in September, not November.
Rep progression: rebuild with 6-8 reps, transition primary work toward 4-6 reps in Sep-Oct, 2-4 reps in Nov, controlled heavy singles before the test while retaining backoff volume. Thanksgiving week is the first test window; attempt only after a clean 205x3 or 210x2.

PACE ANALYSIS 8/31: see the same note on squat-315. Short version - bench peak-to-peak gained +5.8 e1RM in twelve months (210.0 Aug 2025 -> 215.8 Aug 2026) and its one continuous above-peak block ran at +0.62/wk. Required to 225 by Dec 1 is 0.70/wk. The deadline is correctly calibrated, NOT conservative. Do not pull it in. Squat can be pulled to Nov 15; bench cannot.

BENCH RE-TEST SCHEDULED FOR 2026-09-20 (set 8/31). Adam pushed back on the conservative read with two claims. Checked both: CONSISTENCY - he is right, and it materially weakens the Mar-May analogue. Sessions/month went Mar 11, Apr 15, May 8 -> Jul 21, Aug 20, roughly double. The +0.62/wk block ran at half the current training frequency, so it probably understates what bench can do now. EATING - not supported. August closed days average 2,976 against the 3,200 target, 224/day short, with 8 of 24 days under 2,800 and a cumulative shortfall of 5,373 kcal. Scale was FLAT 76.7kg 7/15 -> 76.7kg 8/16; the rise to 77.2 by 8/31 follows creatine starting 8/21 and is mostly water. Observed ~0.17 lb/wk against a 0.5 target.
WHY THE DEADLINE HOLDS ANYWAY: bench has been above its all-time peak for exactly ONE session. There is no data on what it does above peak at 20 sessions/month - 8/31 is the first point on that curve, and a forecast off one point is not a forecast. ON 9/20, after three or four more above-peak sessions, re-run the block analysis. IF bench is beating 1.5 e1RM/wk above peak, PULL DEC 1 IN. If it is tracking nearer 0.6-0.7/wk, the deadline was right and the conversation is closed.
THE LEVER IS THE FLOOR, NOT THE PROGRAMMING. Training frequency is already solved; the surplus is not. Enforced in code 8/31: HealthClient.nutrition() now emits a FLOOR note whenever logged days in the last 21 fall under target-200, with the count, the worst day and the cumulative shortfall in kcal and pounds-not-built.

instrumental to bench-225; keep lean-ish. RETARGETED 8/15: scale flat Jul 15-Aug 15 (76.7->76.5kg) on ~2,950 target; empirical TDEE 2,865 (18 logged days/21d window, observed -0.2 lb/wk). New target 3,200 kcal (~TDEE+335, ~0.65 lb/wk ceiling), protein 150-155g in 4+ feedings, fat ~75g, carbs fill. Recompute PUSHED to ~Sep 15 (was Sep 1): creatine started 8/21 (5g/day, see profile.supplements) and its ~1-2 lb water gain lands inside the Sep 1 window, which would inflate the apparent surplus and wrongly trigger a calorie cut. Run the recompute on a window starting ~Sep 5, once water has plateaued; ignore the 8/21-8/23 weigh-ins as trend data. PINNED 8/28 via targetKcalOverride: 3,200 is now enforced in code, not just prose. Before this the served target had already drifted to 3,080 — with the scale flat, empirical TDEE collapses to average logged intake, so every missed/low day ratchets the next day's target down. Remove the override only when deliberately re-targeting. Prior note (Iraki/Morton split) still governs macro shape.

STATUS 9/2 (legs, 235 THIRD time as prescribed): 235 x 8,6 - 14 reps, up one from the 13 of both prior sessions. e1RM 297.7, back to the 8/26 all-time peak from 289.8. Target 8,7 NOT earned; 235 goes a FOURTH time. 235 now reads 8,5 / 7,6 / 8,6 - identical to the last three of 225's four sessions (6,6 / 7,6 / 8,6 / 8,7), which then paid 25 e1RM on the jump. Hold the line: 235 until 8,7, then 245. Against Nov 15 the gates are ~295 by Oct 1 (cleared, 297.7 today), ~305 by Oct 20, 315-ready by Nov 10. Required rate from 297.7 to 315 by Nov 15 falls to ~1.65/wk. Fuel this session was the corrected version of 8/29 (toast 1.5h out at 14:30, lift 16:00 off the standup, ~1,800 kcal in before training) and the first set went 7 -> 8 - consistent with the 8/29 dip being a fueling/timing reading. ACCESSORIES 9/2: calves 500 x 8,8,7 flat (repeat); hamstring curl 140 x 8,7,5, three sets landed this time (repeat 140, no 145 until 8,8,8); quad extension 145 x 8,6 first outing (repeat 145).

DEADLINE PULLED IN 8/31, 2027-01-01 -> 2026-11-15, at Adam's request and on the pace analysis below. Requires 2.32 e1RM/wk from 289.8, which is 71% of the +3.25/wk he sustained through the Mar-May 2026 block - the one block that ran in genuinely novel territory. Nov 1 was the stretch option and was NOT taken: it needs 2.84/wk and leaves no margin. Reverting is one field edit. The gates move with it: ~295 by Oct 1 (already three weeks ahead), ~305 by Oct 20, 315-ready by Nov 10. The REP TRANSITION DOES NOT MOVE - 315 still requires the 6-8 -> 4-6 -> 2-4 -> singles progression and a clean 285x3 or 295x2 before any attempt, and pulling the date in compresses that, so the drop to 4-6 reps should start in mid-September rather than October.

Primary deadline Jan 1, 2027, aligned with reaching ~180 lb on the 0.5 lb/wk lean bulk. Stretch test Dec 1, 2026 only if 285x3 or 295x2 and a clean 305 single are achieved first. Pace by e1RM: regain ~285 by Sep 1, reach ~295 by Oct 1, ~305 by Nov 15, and become 315-ready by Dec 15. Rebuild in the 6-8 rep range, then transition primary work toward 4-6 reps, 2-4 reps, and finally heavy singles while retaining controlled backoff volume.

STATUS 8/29 (legs, 235 repeat as prescribed): 235 x 7,6 — thirteen reps, exactly the thirteen of 8/26 (8,5) redistributed. e1RM 289.8, DOWN from 297.7 on 8/26. Still clears the Sep 1 gate (285) and sits three weeks ahead of the Oct 1 gate (295). Required rate to 315 by Jan 1 is ~1.42 e1RM/wk against a trailing actual far above it — squat is not the goal at risk, bench is.
THE RULE STANDS: 235 was to be repeated until 8,6 or 8,7. It came back 7,6. DO NOT JUMP TO 245 — take 235 a third time and target 8,7. This is the same consolidation shape as bench 165 (7/30: 6,4 -> 8/16: 8,7) and squat 225, which sat for four sessions and then paid 25 e1RM. Two flat sessions at a new load is the normal middle of that, not a stall.
ACCESSORIES 8/29: Calf raises 500 x 8,8,7 (up from 8,8,5 — repeat 500, third set still owes a rep). Unilateral quad extension 140 x 8,8 COMPLETE — goes to 145. Hamstring curl: jumped 135 -> 145, failed at 4, dropped to 140 for 7,5. The prescription was 140 x 3 x 6-8. This is the bench error in a different lift — buying load ahead of the reps, and it cost a whole set (two logged, three prescribed). Next session: 140 for three sets, no 145 until 140 is 8,8,8.
CONTEXT: session moved 15:00 -> 12:45 straight off a phone call, ~80g carbs 1.75h out, HRV 41.0 on 8/27 (2nd-lowest in series). A flat repeat under those conditions is a fueling/recovery reading, not a load reading.

PACE ANALYSIS 8/31 (Adam asked whether both goals can be pulled in). Computed from the full e1RM series in weights.json, splitting the log into continuous training blocks (no gap >21d) so regain is not mistaken for gain.
THE DECISIVE FACT: both lifts are at ALL-TIME e1RM peaks right now - bench 215.8 (8/31), squat 297.7 (8/26). Every number before this month was lower. The steep trailing slopes (bench 3.4/wk 21d, squat 4.3/wk 21d) are REGAIN slopes off the 36-48 day May-June layoff, and that tailwind ended this month. Forward rates must be read off blocks that ended ABOVE the prior peak, not off the rebuild.
BENCH, rate by block: Jun-Jul25 +1.69/wk (from 186, regain) | Aug-Oct25 -2.23/wk (started AT the 210 peak, went BACKWARDS) | Mar-May26 +0.62/wk (70d, 12 sessions, continuous, 198->204, peaked 209) | Jun-Aug26 +5.06/wk (from 171, pure regain). The Mar-May26 block is the honest analogue for novel territory: +0.62/wk. Peak-to-peak, bench went 210.0 (Aug 2025) -> 215.8 (Aug 2026) = +5.8 e1RM IN TWELVE MONTHS. Required rate to 225 by Dec 1 is 0.70/wk. That is not a conservative deadline - it is almost exactly Adam's demonstrated above-peak rate, with no slack. DO NOT PULL BENCH IN.
SQUAT, rate by block: Jan-Feb26 +3.46/wk | Mar-May26 +3.25/wk (61d, 11 sessions, 249->278, peaked 286 - an all-time high AT THE TIME, so this block genuinely ran in novel territory) | Jul-Aug26 +6.94/wk (regain). Peak-to-peak squat went 247 (2025) -> 297.7 (Aug 2026) = +50.7 in twelve months, against bench's +5.8. Squat sustains 3+/wk into new ground; bench does not. SQUAT CAN BE PULLED IN.
Squat required rates from 289.8 on 8/31: Jan 1 = 1.43/wk | Dec 1 = 1.92/wk | Nov 15 = 2.32/wk | Nov 1 = 2.84/wk. Against a demonstrated 3.25/wk. RECOMMEND NOV 15 (71% of demonstrated rate, six weeks earlier than the current Jan 1); Nov 1 is the stretch and leaves no margin.
THE REAL ACCELERANT IS NOT SLOPE, IT IS CONTINUITY. Layoffs >21d in the log: bench had 24d, 64d, 25d, 28d, 36d and squat had 37d, 31d, 28d, 76d, 26d, 30d, 48d since June 2025 - roughly one every 6-8 weeks. The big one is SEASONAL and lands exactly on these deadlines: bench off 2025-10-18 -> 2025-12-21 (64 DAYS, 193->186) and squat off 2025-09-29 -> 2025-12-14 (76 DAYS, 240->216). Bench was ALREADY decaying at -2.23/wk in the block before that layoff. Finishing squat by Nov 15 is therefore risk management, not ambition: it banks the goal BEFORE the window that has cost Adam the lift every year. Nothing done in September matters as much as not losing October.
UNCHANGED CAVEAT: these are all Epley estimates off 6-8 rep sets, and 172 of 172 logged sessions are 6+ reps. A pulled-in squat deadline does NOT pull in the rep transition - 315 still requires the 4-6 / 2-4 / singles progression and a clean 285x3 or 295x2 before any attempt.
